summary: Facepalm: I found four facepalm candidates for 2026-10-11, all institutional ballot errors inside the Oct. 5–11 window. 1) Colorado: about 800,000 ballots in four counties wrongly include the Front Range Passenger Rail tax question (CPR and Gazette). 2) Athens-Clarke County, Ga.: a mailing-list error sends a second absentee ballot to 1,154 voters (CBS News and WSB-TV). 3) Floyd County, Ind.: a programming error leaves a commissioner race off 572 voters' ballots (LPM and WFYI, but WFYI is running LPM's own story). 4) Oxford, Maine: a packaging error at the printer sends out some wrong ballots (Press Herald and WGME). Every quote was checked against the page text I opened. Every story is about an office, none names a politician, and party is null throughout. I couldn't find a facepalm story that wasn't about ballots. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-11 (window Oct 5–11). I'm submitting two candidates, each backed by two pages I opened from different accepted or official publishers, with verbatim quotes checked against the fetched text. (1) Catherine Debrunner set a women's wheelchair marathon world record (1:33:16) at the Chicago Marathon on Oct 11. Sources: NBC Chicago and the Chicago Sun-Times. (2) An MIT-led team reported in Nature Astronomy on Oct 5 the first observed low-mass star slowly and steadily feeding on a brown dwarf. Sources: MIT News and ScienceDaily. Note that Illinois was also the genius state on Oct 4. The search tool limit was reached before I could add a third, independently sourced alternate. Pair published.

candidates.reason: Already set aside: a possible addiction issue, and no accepted source was found.

candidates.headline: NC State team demonstrates first plasma-filament antenna made with a laser
candidates.reason: Too old. NC State's release is dated Oct. 5, but its own note says the IEEE Journal of Microwaves paper was published Sept. 1.

candidates.headline: Vienna team builds first self-stabilizing thorium nuclear clock (Nature)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The work is from TU Wien in Austria.

candidates.headline: JWST and MeerKAT trace the most distant fast radio burst (Science, Oct. 8)
candidates.reason: Not US-led. Space.com quotes a co-leader at the Sydney Institute for Astronomy, and the burst was detected by MeerKAT in South Africa.

candidates.headline: USGS-led Science study of Kilauea's episodic lava fountains (HI, Oct. 8)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted page could be opened (Science News, which is paywalled and failed a quote check before). The phys.org and Science DOI pages could not be fetched, so there is no second source.

candidates.headline: Taylor Knibb wins the 2026 Ironman World Championship in Kailua-Kona, Hawaii
candidates.reason: The Star-Advertiser page could not be fetched. The other coverage found (NBC Sports, Triathlete, TRI247, Hawaii News Now, Yahoo) is not on the accepted list. It is also a title win rather than a record.

candidates.headline: Galen Rupp sets a U.S. masters marathon record and Emma Grace Hurley runs the fastest U.S. women's debut in Chicago
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source (NBC Chicago). The Sun-Times race reports don't mention either, and the other coverage found (NBC Sports, FloTrack) is not accepted.

candidates.headline: Marcel Hug breaks his own Chicago Marathon wheelchair course record
candidates.reason: Same event as the Debrunner candidate, and it is only a course record. The sources also give different unofficial times (1:21:34 vs 1:21.33).

candidates.headline: Caltech/Yale method predicts the Kondo effect in real materials (Science)
candidates.reason: The journal reference (Science vol. 393, issue 6810) points to an earlier issue, so the publication date is not inside the window.

candidates.headline: PPPL maps a lower-energy route to fusion ignition (Physical Review Letters)
candidates.reason: A theoretical 'may have found' result, and the publication date was not confirmed inside the window.
